title: Add transfer reversals
description:
Adds `POST /transfers/:id/reverse` (scope `transfers:write`), which undoes a posted transfer by posting the same amount back from its destination to its source.

- The reversal is an ordinary transfer posted through `postTransfer`, so the usual rules apply: both accounts open, same currency, and a wallet cannot go below zero (422 if the destination has already spent the funds).
- Migration 0009 adds `transfers.reversal_of` (tenant-scoped foreign key to the original, partial index for the lookup). `reversal_of` is included in the transfer JSON and in event payloads.
- A transfer can be reversed only once, and a reversal cannot itself be reversed; both answer 409 with the related transfer id in the details.
- Besides the reversal's own `transfer.posted`, a new `transfer.reversed` event is written on the original transfer's aggregate, so webhook consumers following the original see it.
- An optional `description` overrides the default "Reversal of transfer <id>". No Idempotency-Key is needed: retrying a reversal that went through gets the 409.

Tests: test/api/reversals.test.ts (balances and entries, description, single reversal, reversal of a reversal, insufficient funds, outbox events, scope and tenant isolation). README updated.

bugs.summary: The already-reversed check reads reversal_of before any lock is taken, under READ COMMITTED, so two concurrent reversals of one transfer both pass it and both post: the money is moved back twice.
bugs.trigger: Two concurrent POST /transfers/:id/reverse for the same transfer, with a destination that can pay the amount twice (a funded wallet or a system account).
bugs.false_rebuttal: Two reversals of the same transfer cannot both go through: reverseTransfer locks both accounts with accounts.lockAccounts (SELECT … FOR UPDATE, ascending id order) before postTransfer runs, so the second reversal waits on the account rows until the first commits and then fails the reversal check with a 409.
